0.title: Math is Mine
0.objective: I can describe the ways we are all doers of math, and compare my math story with a classmate's.

1.title: Math is Exploring and Thinking
1.objective: I can make sense of a problem, plan a strategy, and use fractions of a whole number to compare quantities.

2.title: Math is In My World
2.objective: I can represent a real-world situation with a tape diagram or table and use decimal operations to solve it.

3.title: Math is Explaining and Sharing
3.objective: I can construct an argument using equations, drawings, or words, and use volume to defend a recommendation.

4.title: Math is Finding Patterns
4.objective: I can find patterns and pattern rules, use them to make generalizations, and check my solutions with a table of values.

5.title: Math is Ours
5.objective: I can describe my problem-solving process, name strategies for getting unstuck, and identify the behaviors that make our class a community of math thinkers.

6.title: Understand Statistical Questions
6.objective: I can tell the difference between a statistical question and a non-statistical question.

7.title: Represent and Describe Data in a Histogram
7.objective: I can make and read a histogram to display data in intervals.

8.title: Describe the Data Using the Median
8.objective: I can find the median of a data set and use it to describe what is typical.

9.title: Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot
9.objective: I can make and read a box plot to summarize a data set.

10.title: Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range
10.objective: I can find the range and the interquartile range of a data set and use them to describe how spread out the data is.

11.title: Divide Multi-Digit Numbers Using an Algorithm
11.objective: I can divide multi-digit whole numbers and explain the meaning of the quotient and remainder.

12.title: Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm
12.objective: I can divide with decimals by making the divisor a whole number first.

13.title: Describe Data Using the Mean
13.objective: I can determine the mean of a data set, use a target mean to find a missing value, and explain the mean as the fair share and the balance point of the data.

14.title: Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation
14.objective: I can find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) to describe how spread out data is.

15.title: Choose Appropriate Measures
15.objective: I can choose the best measure of center for a data set based on its shape.

16.title: Add and Subtract Decimals
16.objective: I can add and subtract decimals by lining up the place values and the decimal points.

17.title: Multiply Decimals
17.objective: I can multiply decimals and place the decimal point correctly in the product.

18.title: Understand Ratios
18.objective: I can write and describe a ratio that compares two quantities.

19.title: Understand Rates and Unit Rates
19.objective: I can find a unit rate to compare prices and decide the better buy.

20.title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Tables
20.objective: I can use a ratio table to find equivalent ratios.

21.title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Graphs
21.objective: I can graph the values from a ratio table as points on the coordinate plane.

22.title: Compare Ratio Relationships
22.objective: I can compare ratios by finding unit rates or using equivalent ratios.

23.title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements within the Same System
23.objective: I can use ratio reasoning to convert between units within the same measurement system.

24.title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements Between Systems
24.objective: I can use ratio reasoning to convert measurements between the customary and metric systems.

25.title: Solve Problems with Unit Rates
25.objective: I can solve real-world problems by using unit rates to compare options.

26.title: Equivalent Ratios
26.objective: I can find and check equivalent ratios using multiplication and division.

27.title: Convert Measurement Units
27.objective: I can convert measurement units using ratios and conversion factors.

28.title: Understand Percent
28.objective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.

29.title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
29.objective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.

30.title: Estimate the Percent of a Number
30.objective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers.

31.title: Find and Compare with Percentages
31.objective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.

32.title: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
32.objective: I can determine the whole when I know a part and the percent that part represents.

33.title: Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses
33.objective: I can find the area of a parallelogram using base × height.

34.title: Determine the Area of Triangles
34.objective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.

35.title: Determine the Area of Trapezoids
35.objective: I can find the area of a trapezoid using the formula A = ½(b1 + b2) × h.

36.title: Apply Area Concepts to Solve Problems
36.objective: I can find the area of a composite figure by decomposing it into basic shapes, including a regular polygon split into triangles, and adding or subtracting the areas.

37.title: Determine the Volume of Rectangular Prisms
37.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges using length × width × height.

38.title: Represent Three-Dimensional Figures in Two Dimensions
38.objective: I can find the surface area of a solid by using its net.

39.title: Determine Surface Area of Prisms
39.objective: I can find the surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms.

40.title: Determine Surface Area of Pyramids
40.objective: I can find the surface area of a pyramid by adding the base area and the lateral faces.

41.title: Area of Regular Polygons
41.objective: I can find the area of a regular polygon by decomposing it into triangles.

42.title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
42.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism, including ones with fractional edge lengths, using base area × height.

43.title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Whole Numbers
43.objective: I can divide a whole number by a unit fraction and divide a fraction by a whole number by writing the whole number over 1 and using Keep, Change, Flip.

44.title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers
44.objective: I can divide a fraction by a fraction and divide with mixed numbers by multiplying by the reciprocal.

45.title: Explore Numerical Expressions with Exponents
45.objective: I can write and evaluate numbers in exponent form using a base and a power.

46.title: Write and Evaluate Numerical Expressions with Exponents
46.objective: I can write numerical expressions from a real situation and evaluate them using the order of operations, including powers.

47.title: Write and Evaluate Algebraic Expressions
47.objective: I can write an algebraic expression for a real situation and evaluate it for a given value of the variable.

48.title: Identify Equivalent Algebraic Expressions
48.objective: I can show that two expressions are equivalent by simplifying and combining like terms.

49.title: Find Factors and Multiples
49.objective: I can find the greatest common factor and the least common multiple of two numbers, and use each to solve a real problem.

50.title: Generate Equivalent Expressions
50.objective: I can use the commutative, associative, and identity properties to rewrite expressions.

51.title: Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions
51.objective: I can divide a whole number by a fraction by multiplying by the reciprocal.

52.title: Divide Mixed Numbers
52.objective: I can divide mixed numbers by first changing them to improper fractions.

53.title: Fraction Division Problem Solving
53.objective: I can solve real-world problems by writing and solving fraction division equations.

54.title: Least Common Multiple
54.objective: I can find the least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers by listing or comparing their multiples.

55.title: Prime Factorization
55.objective: I can write a number as a product of its prime factors using a factor tree.

56.title: The Distributive Property
56.objective: I can use the distributive property to expand and factor expressions.

57.title: Simplify Algebraic Expressions
57.objective: I can simplify algebraic expressions by combining like terms.

58.title: Explore Integers and Their Opposites
58.objective: I can use integers to represent quantities in everyday life, explain what 0 means in each situation, and name the opposite of an integer on the number line.

59.title: Represent Rational Numbers and Their Opposites on the Number Line
59.objective: I can place rational numbers, including fractions and decimals, on a number line.

60.title: Understand Absolute Value of Rational Numbers
60.objective: I can find the absolute value of a rational number — an integer, fraction, or decimal — as its distance from zero.

61.title: Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers
61.objective: I can compare and order integers using a number line.

62.title: Represent Rational Numbers on the Coordinate Plane
62.objective: I can plot and identify points on the coordinate plane using ordered pairs.

63.title: Determine Distance on the Coordinate Plane
63.objective: I can find the distance between two points on the coordinate plane using absolute value.

64.title: Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane
64.objective: I can draw polygons from their vertex coordinates on the coordinate plane, and use coordinates to find side lengths and solve perimeter and area problems.

65.title: Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants
65.objective: I can plot ordered pairs in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane.

66.title: Reflect Points Across Axes
66.objective: I can reflect points across the x-axis and y-axis on the coordinate plane.

67.title: Understand Equations and Their Solutions
67.objective: I can write an equation for a real situation and check whether a given value is a solution by substituting it.

68.title: Write and Solve Equations Using Addition or Subtraction
68.objective: I can solve one-step addition and subtraction equations using inverse operations.

69.title: Write and Solve Equations Using Multiplication or Division
69.objective: I can solve one-step multiplication and division equations using inverse operations.

70.title: Write and Represent Inequalities
70.objective: I can write inequalities to represent real-world situations.

71.title: Understand Inequalities and Their Solutions
71.objective: I can graph the solutions of an inequality on a number line.

72.title: Solve and Graph Inequalities
72.objective: I can solve an inequality and graph its solution set on a number line.

73.title: Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving
73.objective: I can model and solve real-world problems using equations and inequalities.

74.title: Explore Relationships Between Two Variables
74.objective: I can recognize when two quantities change together, and identify which one is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable.

75.title: Analyze Graphs of Relationships Between Two Variables
75.objective: I can use a table and a graph to determine and analyze the relationship between two variable quantities.

76.title: Write Equations to Represent Relationships Between Two Variables
76.objective: I can write an equation from a table or a graph to model the relationship between the dependent and independent variables.

77.title: Apply Two-Variable Relationships to Solve Problems
77.objective: I can write an equation to represent the relationship between two variable quantities and use it to solve a real problem.

78.title: Math is Everywhere
78.objective: I can find applications of math outside of school — in professions like being a chef, in hobbies like gardening, and around my own house.

79.title: Math is Beauty
79.objective: I can use bilateral symmetry to describe structure in nature and in human creations.

80.title: Math is Playful
80.objective: I can use patterns and relationships to make sense of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle and think logically about its solutions.

81.title: Math is Ingenuity
81.objective: I can use ratios and models to explain how the Penny Farthing and gear-driven bicycles were ingenious solutions to a real problem.

82.title: Math is Boundless
82.objective: I can create and describe geometric designs using repetition, patterns, and rhythm, and use a pattern unit to predict what comes next.

83.title: Math is Mine
83.objective: I can look back at my answers from Lesson 1-1, describe how my math biography has changed this year, and recognize ways we are all doers of math.
